messages:
Monica Patel: Kicking off SDK parity audit. Goal is to stop the “why does Python do X but TS does Y” support churn. Ibrahim is TL. Can we align on (1) parity matrix ownership, (2) what counts as “breaking”, (3) initial gap list to tackle first?

Ibrahim Khan: :wave: thanks Monica. I created the Linear epic ENG-2481 (will link in the project channel too). For parity matrix: I’d like a single source of truth we can review with Platform/SRE/Security. Sabrina — can you own keeping the matrix current (with input from Dana/Mateusz) and tagging questions? I can do final call/merge decisions.

Sabrina James: Yep, I can own the matrix + keep it updated after reviews. Where do we want it living? Drive sheet or Confluence table?

Ibrahim Khan: Drive sheet for now (easier to diff during review). Then we can snapshot key decisions into Confluence once stable.

Wei Chen: +1 to Drive. For docs we’ll need a “final spec” link anyway; but during week 1–2, Drive is easier.

Dana Lo: Works. For TS, I already have a list of deltas vs Python from support threads (streaming disconnect handling, 429 retry behavior, default timeouts). I’ll dump into the sheet once I have the columns.

Mateusz Zielinski: Same for Go. Biggest pain I’ve seen is context cancel vs timeout mapping (callers can’t reliably tell what happened). I’ll add specifics + current behavior.

Leila Farouk: If we’re doing conformance tests later, can we structure the matrix to map to test cases? Like “Auth: env var order”, “Retries: status classifier”, “Streaming: partial frame” etc.

Ibrahim Khan: Yes please. Sabrina can add a “Conformance scenario ID” column (even if it’s TBD) so we don’t lose track.

Sahana Iyer: Also add “CI gate?” column. Some stuff is hard to test deterministically (streaming/proxy edge cases). If we flag those early we can decide whether to mock gateway or allow flaky quarantines.

Sabrina James: Cool. I’ll set up columns: Area (Auth/Retries/Timeouts/Streaming/Errors), Current Py/TS/Go behavior, Proposed target, Breaking? (Y/N), Notes/links, Conformance scenario ID, Owner.

Monica Patel: Great. Next: definition of “breaking”. We need a consistent line for semver + release comms.

Elliot Price: From docs POV: “breaking” is anything that requires customer code change OR changes observed behavior in a way that can impact reliability/cost (e.g. suddenly retries happen when they didn’t). Even if the API surface is same, behavior changes will surprise people.

Dana Lo: Agree. In JS world, behavior default changes *are* breaking in practice even if types don’t change. Example: changing default timeout from “infinite-ish” to 60s will break long requests. Another: enabling retries by default could cause duplicate side-effects if endpoints aren’t idempotent.

Rafael Mendes: +1. SRE view: retries-by-default is dangerous unless we cap budgets + only retry safe cases. If you ship it as a minor and suddenly everyone has retries, you can cause retry amplification + rate-limit spirals.

Ethan Park: Platform note: some endpoints are safe-ish, but we don’t have strong idempotency guarantees across the board today. We can recommend idempotency keys / request-id use, but it’s not universal.

Ibrahim Khan: Proposal for “breaking” labeling in the matrix:
- Breaking = any default behavior change that can materially change request volume, latency, or error semantics (new retries, new timeout, different error class), OR any config/env var rename.
- Non-breaking = bug fix in parsing (unless it changes output / event ordering), additive config options, improved error messages.
Would Security want different bar for auth?

Marcus Lin: For auth, changing the accepted env var names or header name is breaking. Tightening validation can be breaking too (e.g., previously accepted whitespace keys). We should be explicit: standardize key resolution order + header exactly once and provide migration message. Also: do not log secrets (even in debug).

Dev Patel: From support ticket view: biggest “breaking surprise” is when error messages change and customer automation keys off substrings. If we can keep machine-readable codes stable + message improvements additive, that’s better.

Mateusz Zielinski: For Go, error wrapping details matter. Some customers do `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` / `context.DeadlineExceeded`. If we switch to custom error types, that can break. So we should define a stable taxonomy AND preserve standard sentinel checks where possible.

Ibrahim Khan: Noted. For the matrix “Breaking?” column we’ll call out “breaks error inspection patterns” separately.

Monica Patel: Ok. Let’s capture a few initial gaps so we’re aligned on what goes in week 1 audit.

Dana Lo: Initial TS gaps (off top of head):
1) Streaming: we currently treat mid-stream disconnect as “done” in some cases if the last chunk was valid; customers see truncated output with no error.
2) Retries: undici/fetch differences; we retry 429 more aggressively than Python (no respect for Retry-After today).
3) Timeouts: Node runtime default behavior is inconsistent; some calls have no overall timeout.
4) Auth: env var names differ between docs and SDK; also header casing normalization differs.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go gaps:
1) Timeout vs context cancellation surfaced inconsistently (sometimes `context deadline exceeded`, sometimes wrapped net error).
2) Retry classifier: we retry some 5xx but not connection resets (depending on transport). Needs standard.
3) Streaming reader: partial SSE frame handling is fragile (read loop assumes newline boundaries).
4) Request ID: we don’t propagate request-id header into errors/hooks consistently.

Sabrina James: Python gaps (from tickets I’ve seen):
1) Streaming “hangs” behind certain proxies; no read timeout so it looks stuck.
2) Retry defaults: currently minimal; customers build their own and do weird things.
3) Auth error message unclear when env var missing (“NoneType” error in some flows).

Rafael Mendes: Also want a standard retry budget (max attempts AND total time). Backoff must have jitter. And we should never retry streaming by default; at most allow opt-in with explicit semantics.

Ethan Park: Gateway guarantee: we will return `request-id` on responses, and for 429 we often include `retry-after`. Error payload consistency is in flight (I’ll confirm fields). SDK should respect `retry-after` when present.

Ibrahim Khan: Great. Action items:
- Sabrina: create the Drive parity matrix today and share link here + in ENG-2481. Populate initial columns + owners.
- Dana/Mateusz: add current behavior + concrete examples/log links by EOW.
- Ethan/Rafael/Marcus: please add “platform constraints” notes in the matrix (idempotency, retry-after, safe retry boundaries, auth requirements).
- Leila/Sahana: add a “testability” note per row (mockable vs integration-only).

Wei Chen: Once the matrix is live, tag me/Elliot on anything that will require docs/migration language (esp env vars, timeouts, retry defaults). We should start building the migration guide outline early.

Monica Patel: Perfect. Keep the thread updated with the matrix link and any open questions we need to resolve in the kickoff review. :thumbsup:

Sabrina James: Matrix link (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-devex-sdk-parity (sheet inside: “SDK Parity Matrix v1”). Please add notes inline + @mention me on anything that needs triage.

Sahana Iyer: Added “CI gate?” column and a note on streaming tests: we’ll likely need a mocked SSE server + a chaos mode (disconnect mid-frame) to be deterministic.

Ibrahim Khan: Thanks all. Next step is to schedule a 45m review early next week w/ Platform/SRE/Security once we have enough filled in. I’ll send invite.

Marcus Lin: One more: please add a row for “API key sourcing from files” (some SDKs do it today informally). Security prefers env vars + explicit config only; if we support files, it needs clear guidance + safe permissions messaging.

Ibrahim Khan: Good call, adding as an explicit decision point (likely “no” by default).
